comparison: Both affirm the central finding that putrescine regulates Type I pili-dependent surface motility (C6, C14). OpenEval emphasizes convergence of multiple experimental methods, while peer reviewers note the data 'convincingly demonstrate' this role. Strong agreement on core conclusion.

Both support that surface motility depends on pili and not flagella (C3, C33-C42). OpenEval details genetic deletions, EM, and glucose effects. Peer Reviewer 3 explicitly confirms 'the manuscript shows that the surface motility phenotype is dependent on Type I fimbriae.' Strong agreement.

Both strongly support the optimal putrescine concentration requirement (C75-C84). OpenEval emphasizes convergence across motility assays, RT-qPCR, ELISA, and TEM. Peer Reviewer 3 explicitly states 'All experiments converge to the same conclusion that an optimal level of putrescine is needed.' Complete agreement.

Both support putrescine specificity over spermidine (C26, C55-C59). OpenEval highlights rescue experiments demonstrating specificity. Peer reviewers accept the distinction, with Reviewer 2 noting strains 'incapable of synthesizing putrescine' have decreased motility. Strong agreement.

Both support genetic redundancy in putrescine synthesis pathways (C4, C48-C54). OpenEval details systematic deletion analysis. Peer Reviewer 2 states 'The authors characterize the specific polyamine pathways that are important.' Strong agreement on pathway characterization.

Both support that putrescine transporters affect motility (C5, C61-C65). OpenEval details deletion analysis and expression correlations. Peer reviewers accept transport findings as part of pathway characterization. Strong agreement.

Both support the catabolism findings despite mechanistic complexity (C66-C70, C73-C74). OpenEval notes paradoxical results are experimentally sound. Peer reviewers accept findings without challenge, consistent with dose-response relationship. Agreement on experimental observations.

Both support homeostatic compensation in polyamine metabolism (C11, C101-C107, C137, C144). OpenEval details coordinated transcriptional changes. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly states 'The data suggest homeostatic control of polyamine synthesis.' Strong agreement.

Both support metabolic shifts toward putrescine synthesis and away from energy metabolism (C12-C13, C112-C121). OpenEval details RNAseq data on energy genes. Peer Reviewer 3 directly states 'without putrescine, the metabolism of the cell is shifted towards production of putrescine and away from energy metabolism.' Strong agreement.

Both support transcriptional regulation findings including phase variation analysis (C10, C91-C96, C133-C134). OpenEval combines RNAseq with functional validation. Peer Reviewer 2 states 'They rule out potential effects of pilin phase variation.' Strong agreement.

Both support RNAseq findings on pili gene expression (C7-C8, C90, C132). OpenEval notes direct support from RNAseq data. Peer Reviewer 2 states 'RNAseq provides a detailed overview of gene expression in the strain lacking putrescine.' Strong agreement.

Both support RNAseq results on putrescine catabolism genes (C85-C89). OpenEval notes appropriate statistical thresholds and reasonable inference about intracellular levels. Peer reviewers accept RNAseq findings without challenge. Agreement.

Both support that putrescine does not act through phase variation (C9, C99-C100). OpenEval details PCR analysis showing no phase switching. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly states authors 'rule out potential effects of pilin phase variation.' Strong agreement.

Both support high-level interpretations of metabolic competition and resource allocation (C15, C145-C149, C151). OpenEval notes reasonable inferences from transcriptomic data. Peer reviewers accept metabolic shift interpretations. Agreement on interpretive conclusions.

Both support ion transport gene changes and compensatory mechanisms (C108-C111, C138-C143). OpenEval notes speculation is appropriately qualified. Peer reviewers accept as part of homeostatic control findings. Agreement on data, speculation acknowledged.

Both support broader conclusions about polyamine metabolism's role (C122-C131). OpenEval synthesizes genetic analysis into conclusions about rapid adjustment. Peer reviewers accept pathway characterization findings. Agreement on synthesis of results.

Both support that polyamine pathways modulate motility through multiple mechanisms (C124-C126). OpenEval details synthesis, catabolism, and transport. Peer reviewers accept pathway characterization. Agreement.
Both support catabolism findings as part of polyamine metabolism regulation (C129). OpenEval includes catabolism in broader synthesis. Peer reviewers accept dose-response relationship. Agreement.

Both address discrepancies with prior work (C152-C159). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to untested speculation about temperature effects. Peer reviewers accept authors' reconciliation without challenge. Divergence: OpenEval more cautious about speculative mechanism.

Both support comparison with prior work and identification of conserved responses (C160-C167). OpenEval notes reasonable but untested speculation about media effects. Peer reviewers accept comparative findings. Agreement on conserved mechanisms.

Both address the IS1 insertion in fimE (C43-C47). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting reasonable inference about FimE function. Peer Reviewer 3 rates as UNCERTAIN, raising concern about generalizability to other isolates/strains. Significant divergence: peer review questions broader applicability.
